OracleViolation: editor-browser-mixed violated at checkpoint "step1" (law: mixed browser editing history).
Law: For every legal mixed action history, source and selection obey the adopted per-command models after every action, typing/paste use the prior input document, and native undo/redo respects the remaining branch.
Difference: step1.state
History: {"mobile":false,"native":false,"scene":"prose","body":"a","actions":[{"kind":"type","at":"current","a":0,"b":0,"text":"\t100.\n    - a","activation":"click"},{"kind":"indent","at":"end","a":0,"b":0,"text":"α😀 prose","activation":"click"},{"kind":"undo","at":"current","a":0,"b":0,"text":"α😀 prose","activation":"click"},{"kind":"redo","at":"current","a":0,"b":0,"text":"α😀 prose","activation":"click"},{"kind":"type","at":"end","a":0,"b":0,"text":"x","activation":"click"},{"kind":"outdent","at":"end","a":0,"b":0,"text":"α😀 prose","activation":"click"}]}
Authority: Decision by Kyle Mathews (GitHub KyleAMathews),2026-11-18: arbitrary mixed-action browser histories, Unicode/paragraph boundaries and undo followed by a new edit, retaining adopted command guarantees.
Known limits: Twelve actions, bounded source alphabet, full editor; tick-free default code serialization; selected collisions permit any valid literal fence preserving exact body/context and body selection. Native undo only on native changed-source transactions up to no-op/DOM-paste boundaries; no native undo after forced fallback. No arbitrary Markdown, OS clipboard or preview claim; undo caret is unconstrained.
